- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if 3–5 consecutive days show price retracing to prior range, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
